messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: gpu-queue-depth (prod-us-east-1) exceeded 95% for 6m. 120s avg queue length 42. Top affected model: open-eval-7b. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/infr/queues/prod-us-east-1

alex.huang: paging oncall. I can take first look.

priya.rao: I'm on my way, grabbing logs and recent deploys. Any customers showing 429s?

jamal.singh: Customer telemetry shows increased latency and throttling for endpoint /v1/generate/stream. A handful of high-traffic tenants hit per-tenant rate caps.

casey_oncall: got the PagerDuty. Oncall switching to alex -> casey. @alex.huang please post if you need escalation.

alex.huang: quick check: autoscale-gpu reports attempted scale to 24 nodes but failed due to "scale_limit_reached" on the ASG side. current desired=24, max=24.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler: Scale request queued. Reason: pool-driver-errors increasing. Health checks failing on 6/18 newly launched GPU nodes.

sasha_k: looking at node logs: repeated driver crashes. Kernel reports multiple "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 27411" and OOM kills of process "inference-runtime". Node flapping ~reboot cycle 2-3m.

priya.rao: Xid 79 commonly points to GPU driver/firmware instability under heavy durable kernels. Which kernel/driver version on the pool?

alex.huang: pool image: redwood-gpu-ubuntu-22.04@nvdriver-525.89.02 + cudnn-8.4. Verified yesterday during rollout. Recent deploy?

jamal.singh: there was a small runtime change 2 hours ago toggling aggressive prefetch in KV cache. Might increase memory pressure.

casey_oncall: mitigation plan options: 1) scale up max temporarily to drain queue (but ASG limit is org-wide) 2) disable new node autoscaling and use existing healthy nodes 3) roll nodes to older driver or patch 4) fall back traffic to smaller model variant / lower concurrency. Thoughts?

alex.huang: immediate: reduce incoming concurrency for heavy tenants (throttle) and route traffic to fallback model open-eval-3b where latency ok. I'll open a short-lived rate-limit rule.

priya.rao: I'll mark flappy nodes unschedulable: kubectl taint nodes -l role=gpu pool=prod-us-east-1:NoSchedule and drain pods from unhealthy nodes. Then restart nvidia-driver service on nodes that come back, collecting dmesg output.

sasha_k: paste of recent dmesg snippets:
```
[  842.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=27411, fault: block
[  842.123460] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 27411 (inference-runti) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

jamal.singh: we're seeing KV cache prefetcher allocating large pinned GPU memory, then runtime OOM. If nodes are flapping, autoscaler sees them unhealthy and keeps trying to replace, hitting ASG cap.

casey_oncall: I've requested an emergency increase of ASG max from infra (ticket #INC-5921) but ETA ~20m. Meanwhile we should reduce demand. Sasha, can you toggle the prefetch flag off in runtime config for the 7b model?

sasha_k: yes and pushing change to canary routing now: set PREFETCH_ENABLED=false for open-eval-7b on prod-us-east-1. Rolling update patch applied to 10% of traffic.

alex.huang: applying tenant-level throttles for 3 noisy tenants now: commands pasted in #devex-runbook. Throttles should cut incoming QPS by ~50% — expecting queue depth to drop.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler: new desired=18 after node cordon/drain. 4 new nodes failed health checks; scaling paused.

priya.rao: manual actions: cordoned 6 nodes, drained pods, rebooted 4. After reboot, restarted nvidia drivers via systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service and collected /var/log/syslog -> uploaded to incident artifacts. two nodes still showing Xid 13 and kernel panic; isolating them.

jamal.singh: customer support note: contacted top 5 affected customers with ETA ~30m and mitigation steps. Logged as high impact.

casey_oncall: we should add a scaledown-protection override for healthy nodes so autoscaler doesn't replace them while we stabilize. Requesting ops to set annotation redwood/scale-protect=true on these nodes.

alex.huang: traffic on fallback open-eval-3b looks steady, latency back to SLO for most users, but cost per token increased. Good temporary tradeoff. Queue depth trending down from 42 -> 12 in last 7m.

sasha_k: idea for long term: add driver watchdog that blacklists kernel/driver combos that produce Xid > threshold and pins autoscaler to use previously known-good AMIs. Filing follow-up: ENG-DRV-125.

priya.rao: root cause hypothesis: aggressive KV prefetch change combined with driver/firmware corner-case causes GPU OOMs -> node reboots -> autoscaler replacing nodes until ASG cap hit -> effective capacity drop and queue growth. Need to rollback prefetch change and validate on canary with driver upgrades.

autoscale-bot: Alert: ASG max capacity reached for prod-gpu-asg (limit 24). Request to increase submitted.

casey_oncall: summary & action items:
- short-term: throttles + fallback model (completed)
- triage: cordon/drain/restart drivers on flappy nodes (in progress)
- infra: ASG max increase request (in flight)
- follow-up: revert prefetch change + driver compatibility tests (ENG-ML + ENG-RUNTIME)
- postmortem: include customer impact and timeline

jamal.singh: I'll own the postmortem and link artifacts. Assigning to ENG-ML for the config rollback and ENG-RUNTIME for driver test matrix.

alex.huang: queue depth now 8, new healthy node joins + canary changes look stable. Leaving this thread open until full stabilization and ASG confirmed increased. Please update here with any further regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=high, incident_id=INC-2026-1748078642. PagerDuty incident remains open.
text: PROD GPU queue surge + driver instability -> autoscale hit ASG cap; throttles, fallbacks, node cordons, driver restarts, ASG increase request, follow-up tasks assigned
